rationale: C22 provides a concrete drafting pattern closely matching the child: it assigns military-benefit administration to service secretaries, requires interservice conformity so far as practicable, preserves existing regulations until replaced, and supersedes an earlier order. C07 contains nearly the same machinery but lacks C22's express supersession provision. C03 also combines uniformity of regulations with continuation of prior rules, but in a less closely parallel setting. The convergence and sequence in C22 are materially stronger than generic administrative boilerplate.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The regulations of the Secretary of the Navy and the regulations of the Secretary of the Army and the Secretary of the Air Force with respect to the award of the Purple Heart shall, so far as practicable, be of uniform application
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The quantity and kind of clothing, and any cash allowances in lieu thereof, prescribed by the Secretary of the Treasury hereunder with respect to the Coast Guard and the Coast Guard Reserve shall, so far as practicable, be in conformity with those prescribed by the Secretary of Defense with respect to the Navy and Naval Reserve
shared_material.explanation: Both impose practical uniformity across military services in administering the same personnel benefit.

shared_material.child_excerpt: existing regulations issued pursuant to that order shall, so far as they are not inconsistent with this order, remain in effect until modified or revoked by regulations issued by the Secretary of the Navy pursuant to this order
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Existing regulations prescribing the quantity and kind of clothing furnished, and any cash allowances in lieu thereof, shall remain in effect until modified, revoked, or superseded by action taken pursuant to this order.
shared_material.explanation: The child closely follows the parent's transitional machinery preserving existing regulations pending replacement under the new order.

shared_material.child_excerpt: This order shall supersede [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of December 3, 1941
shared_material.parent_excerpt: This order shall become effective on April 1, 1950, and on that date shall supersede [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE]
shared_material.explanation: Both expressly replace an earlier directive while modernizing military personnel-benefit rules.
